data.title: A hit says how much of the question it holds, not how far ahead it is
data.why: The failure that matters is a confidently wrong passage: 28 of 100 paraphrased questions returned one. The obvious signal was the margin between the first hit and the second, and measurement killed it - 0.10 when the top hit is right against 0.08 when it is wrong, so any threshold would have flagged more than half the correct answers, and a warning that cries wolf is ignored. Coverage separates because it is not about ranking at all: it is how much of what was asked is present in the record, weighted by rarity. 1.00 against 0.62 at the median; at 0.7 it catches two thirds of the wrong answers and misfires on a fifth of the right ones.
data.rejected: The score gap between the first hit and the second: measured, and it does not distinguish a right answer from a wrong one.; A confidence label instead of a number: the number is honest about being a measurement, and an agent can pick its own threshold.
